# Implementation plan — issue #4701

Planning ref: `main` at `66707437b53aa54446d661c8f409795577d13ead`. No integration branch was specified, so there is no stated ref mismatch. The `/answer [auto-answered-by-clarify]` maps to the clarifier’s finding that no questions were needed; it supplies no additional design choice.

Scope-mode: Selective Expansion  
Reuse-audit: extends `_has_active_autofix_run`, `_load_actions_runs_cached`, and the merge train’s release snapshot  
Scope-mode justification: Changing dispatches 1–3 alone would leave default-branch runs invisible to recovery and duplicate-dispatch guards. Include the directly affected lookups and empty-commit guards, while leaving the separately tracked post-commit retrigger to #4898. This is the complete safe scope, rather than a ≤30-LOC/≤10-minute shortcut: under `unattended_system_instructions.md` §6, Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed.

## Automation integration

Extend existing scripts and workflows only. The poller’s `*/5` schedule, PR-close merge-train release, and `stable`-push forward-merge workflow remain the entry points. No new script, supervisor, database gate, schedule, or future-removal registry entry is needed. Target an implementation and focused-check budget of **≤60 minutes**.

## Files likely to change

- `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`: conflict dispatch and PR-named-run detection in the retrigger, stall-judge, and directly affected empty-commit guards.
- `scripts/review_merge_train.sh`: release dispatch and its existing active-run snapshot.
- `.github/workflows/forward-merge-stable-to-main.yml`: fallback dispatch and now-inaccurate head-ref comments.
- `workflow-templates/ai-review.yml`: dispatched-run PR name; retain `.github/workflows/internal-review.yml`’s existing name.
- `tests/test_conflict_dispatch_active_run_visibility.py`, `tests/test_review_merge_train.py`, and `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`: focused contract and behavioral coverage.
- `agents.md`: correct its forward-merge head-ref-dispatch description.
- `changelog.d/4701-review-dispatch-default-branch.md`: a `<!-- changelog: security -->` fragment; do not edit `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Functions and behavior

1. Validate a positive decimal PR number before `_dispatch_review_for_conflicts`, `_mt_dispatch_review`, or the forward-merge fallback dispatches. Remove `--ref`; pass only the PR number and the existing normalized `allow_workflow_edits` input. Retain each site’s warning and failure-recovery behavior. `gh workflow run` without `--ref` selects the remote default-branch workflow; `--ref` selects the workflow version at that ref. ([cli.github.com](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_workflow_run?utm_source=openai))
2. Add `AI Review [pr:<N>]` as the consumer wrapper’s `workflow_dispatch` run name. Reuse the internal wrapper’s existing `Internal: AI Review & Autofix [pr:<N>]` name. Recognize either exact title **only** on the corresponding review workflow’s dispatched runs; retain legacy head-branch matching. Use the existing REST snapshot fields (`event`, `display_title`, `path`, including paths with an `@ref` suffix) and, for a direct miss-path lookup, one bounded `gh run list --event workflow_dispatch` request with `displayTitle`, `workflowName`, `status`, `conclusion`, `createdAt`, and `databaseId`. These fields and filters are supported by the GitHub CLI and Actions run API. ([cli.github.com](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_run_list?utm_source=openai))
3. Extend `_has_active_autofix_run`’s current miss-path lookup rather than adding a second PR-named query. In retrigger recovery, account for a matching active PR-named run and compare applicable completed outcomes by recency: an older failed branch run must not override newer work. Make `invoke_stall_judge` find matching runs in its already-loaded `_load_actions_runs_cached` blob.
4. Make both empty-commit guards recognize PR-named active runs in that blob. If the cache misses before a push, extend the existing direct check with **at most one additional PR-named-run call**, made only after its head-branch lookup misses; preserve its freshness window and fail-open diagnostics.
5. Make the merge train’s **single** release snapshot key eligible active runs by `pr:<N>` as well as by legacy head branch. Preserve its release claim, label restoration, and API-failure behavior; do not add a per-queued-PR lookup.

## Data structures affected

Only in-memory run matching changes: a PR key alongside the existing branch key. No persistent schema, label, environment variable, or workflow input changes. Document any shared lookup’s accepted run shape, returned result, one-call miss-path bound, and behavior when a listing is unavailable.

## API/interface changes

The consumer wrapper gains an additive, visible run name for dispatched runs. Existing dispatch inputs stay unchanged. Keep using `gh workflow run`: unlike that CLI’s default-branch behavior, the REST workflow-dispatch endpoint requires an explicit `ref`. ([cli.github.com](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_workflow_run?utm_source=openai))

## Security considerations

The trust boundary is PR-derived data reaching a write-permitted, secret-inheriting review workflow. A workflow-created forward-merge branch is still cut from `stable`, whose workflow copy may differ from the default branch; do not exempt it. Reject missing, zero, or malformed PR numbers, and never use a PR head ref to select executable workflow code. An exact run title is **correlation data, not authorization**: constrain matching by dispatch event and review workflow, and never let an unrelated or PR-titled run authorize a merge. No new endpoint or permission grant is proposed.

## Risks and edge cases

- **Codebase conflict:** `tests/test_conflict_dispatch_active_run_visibility.py` currently requires the forward-merge `--ref`; `tests/test_review_merge_train.py` and `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py` likewise assert head-ref dispatch. Change these assertions with the behavior.
- The existing run snapshot is bounded and may omit a run; preserve miss-path checks where an empty-commit push could invalidate active editing. Unavailable listings must not be reported as a confirmed absence.
- Consumer PR-name matching becomes available when the updated wrapper is installed; legacy branch matching must continue to work meanwhile.
- The comments report earlier work on a Claude project branch and draft PR #4709, but that branch is not in this planning checkout. Reconcile that work before implementation to avoid duplication. The comments assign the post-commit retrigger to #4898.

## Decisions

### D1 — Dispatch from the default branch at all three sites
- **Chosen:** Remove `--ref`, including at the workflow-created forward-merge fallback.
- **Alternatives considered:** Exempt that branch or separately resolve and pin a trusted workflow SHA.
- **Why:** One rule closes the executable-workflow trust boundary without another lookup.

### D2 — Preserve both run-identity paths
- **Chosen:** Add exact PR-named dispatch matching to existing snapshots and bounded miss-path lookups; keep branch matching.
- **Alternatives considered:** Query Actions separately for every PR in each recovery loop.
- **Why:** Existing data covers the common path without per-PR API fanout or losing older-run compatibility.

## Testing considerations

Extend the three existing test modules to cover all dispatch sites, invalid PR numbers, both wrapper names, unrelated or spoofed titles, `queued`/`pending`/`in_progress` runs, newer-run ordering, stall-judge cache input, both empty-commit guards, `@ref` paths, and lookup/dispatch failures. Run focused tests, applicable pinned repository lint/workflow checks, and the workflow file-size guard. No validator was run and no repository file was changed during planning.

## Pre-execution self-check

The requested sites, trust boundary, automation entry points, compatibility path, and tests are identified. The reported prior project work needs reconciliation, but the issue is implementable from this planning ref.
